workflow.label: Automation starter plan
workflow.question: How defined is the process today?
stages: It changes or lives in people’s heads
The steps are clear, but manual
We already have tools to connect
directions: Map the process before buying automation.
actions: Document the trigger, owner and exception path using one real example.
Measure current handling time and choose one success measure for a pilot.
Confirm API access, permissions and a manual fallback for each connected tool.
focusActions: Trace one enquiry from arrival to an assigned CRM owner.
Pick one repeated request and list the approvals it needs.
Choose one report, its source systems and who approves the summary.
Choose one repeated task with a clear input and finish line.
workflow.checkpoint: Decide which actions always require a person’s approval.
workflow.bring: A process example, the tools involved and an approximate weekly volume.
workflow.deliverable: A first-workflow checklist with the next decision to make.
workflow.fitTitle: One repeatable process. One accountable owner.
workflow.metric: Handling time, corrections and exception rate

whatsapp.label: WhatsApp chatbot starter plan
whatsapp.question: Where are you starting from?
stages: An idea or personal WhatsApp number
Business Platform access and a CRM
directions: Define the conversation before connecting a bot.
Pilot a narrow FAQ and handoff flow.
actions: List approved answers and assess Business Platform setup with your account owner.
Test common questions, unknown answers and an explicit request for a person.
Check API permissions, duplicate handling and who owns the conversation after handoff.
focusActions: List the customer questions the assistant can answer and when it must stop.
Write the minimum questions needed to route a sales enquiry.
Separate a booking request from a confirmed calendar appointment.
Choose one conversation type and define its useful next step.
whatsapp.checkpoint: Agree the human handoff and check applicable messaging requirements before launch.
whatsapp.bring: Five common questions, your current WhatsApp setup and the destination for enquiries.
whatsapp.deliverable: A conversation checklist with setup and handoff priorities.
whatsapp.proofLabel: Related enquiry-flow work, not a WhatsApp deployment
whatsapp.fitTitle: Recurring questions. A team ready to take over.
whatsapp.metric: Useful enquiry details and successful human handoffs

mvp.label: AI MVP starter plan
mvp.question: How far along is your idea?
directions: Validate the user problem before the feature list.
Test reliability before adding more features.
actions: Describe the user, the job they need done and how they handle it today.
Define the smallest end-to-end release and explicitly exclude the rest.
Turn feedback and failure examples into acceptance tests for the next release.
focusActions: Write one user story and the result the user should leave with.
Identify the biggest failure mode in the existing prototype.
Separate the AI task from the interface and rules around it.
Choose one assumption the first release needs to test.
mvp.checkpoint: Use realistic inputs to evaluate output quality, latency and recurring model costs.
mvp.bring: A target user, one core use case and any non-confidential prototype or feedback.
mvp.deliverable: A first-release checklist with a scope boundary and evaluation checkpoint.
mvp.fitTitle: A specific user. A problem worth testing.
mvp.metric: Task completion, AI quality and user feedback

documents.label: Document automation starter plan
documents.question: What do you have ready?
stages: An extraction tool that needs improvement
directions: Define the document and its output first.
Run a field-level pilot before integration.
actions: Choose one repeated document type and list the exact fields you need.
Prepare representative, redacted samples and agree field-level acceptance criteria.
Review incorrect and missing values by layout, scan quality and field type.
focusActions: Separate header totals from line items and define reconciliation checks.
Mark required fields and decide how incomplete forms should be handled.
Attach a source reference to each extracted field or finding.
Define a consistent output schema for one document family.
documents.checkpoint: Keep uncertain results in a human review queue before they reach another system.
documents.bring: Document types, approximate volume and required fields. No confidential files needed to enquire.
documents.deliverable: A pilot checklist with data requirements and review checkpoints.
documents.proofLabel: Related structured-workflow work, not an OCR benchmark
documents.fitTitle: Repeated documents. A clear definition of correct.
documents.metric: Field-level quality, correction time and processing cost

property.label: Property enquiry starter plan
property.question: How ready is your enquiry process?
stages: We need to define the buyer journey
Project information and a sales owner
A CRM and an existing lead flow
directions: Test lead ownership and visit requests.
actions: Choose one project and approve what the assistant may say about it.
Agree the buyer requirements to collect and when a sales person takes over.
Validate CRM field mapping, duplicates and who confirms each site visit.
focusActions: Create a maintained source for one project’s approved information.
Define how buyer requirements map to the properties your team handles.
Separate service enquiries from buying or renting enquiries.
Choose one buyer journey and its sales handoff.
property.checkpoint: Never imply live prices, availability or confirmed visits without a reliable source.
property.bring: One project or service, your enquiry channels and the person responsible for follow-up.
property.deliverable: A buyer-journey checklist with qualification and routing priorities.
property.metric: Lead completeness, routing reliability and follow-up quality

automation.label: AI automation starter plan
automation.question: Where are you with automation?
stages: Exploring what AI can help with
A repeated task we want to improve
directions: Find a useful business problem first.
actions: Document the trigger, owner and exception path using one real example.
Measure current handling time and choose one success measure for a pilot.
Confirm API access, permissions and a manual fallback for each connected tool.
focusActions: Trace one lead from arrival to a useful next step for sales.
Choose one document or request and define its correct output.
List approved answers and the questions that need a person.
Choose a repeated task with a clear input, owner and outcome.
automation.checkpoint: Decide which actions always require a person’s approval.
automation.bring: A process example, the tools involved and an approximate weekly volume.
automation.deliverable: A first-pilot checklist with the business outcome, boundaries and next decision.
automation.fitTitle: AI that fits the way your business works.
automation.metric: Time spent, output quality and successful handoffs
